title: Hildegard's music
hookLine: she wrote music still sung, including a sung drama of the virtues where only the devil can't sing
tomorrow: keep each poet's name on the line, or blend them all like honey?

lines: THE VILLAIN USUALLY GETS THE BEST SONG.
A SOUL BETWEEN VIRTUES AND DEVIL.
cards: In a lot of musicals the villain gets the best song. Hildegard did the opposite. She wrote a sung drama called the Ordo Virtutum, the Play of the Virtues.

A human soul is pulled between the Virtues and the Devil, wanders off with him, and comes back wounded, and the Virtues welcome her home. Every part in it is sung, the soul, the Virtues, all of them. Except one.
The Devil never gets a single note. He only shouts. Why would a composer take the music away from her villain?

teach.h: A BURIAL, AND AN ORDER TO DIG.
teach.b: Her answer shows up in a fight late in her life. Hildegard's community buried a young nobleman who had once been excommunicated. She said he had been reconciled before he died.
Church officials in Mainz ordered the body dug up. She refused.
So her whole house was put under an interdict: no Mass, and no singing. The nuns could only say their prayers quietly.
Hildegard wrote the officials a letter, and it's really a teaching on music. Before the fall, she says, Adam's voice joined the praise of the angels.
Music is how people remember that lost harmony, and how they join it again. The Devil, she writes, hates that sound, and works to silence it.
So anyone who silences praise without good cause should ask whose work they're doing. There's the answer to the puzzle. For Hildegard, singing God's praise isn't decoration.
It's heaven's harmony, the thing the Devil walked away from. He can shout.

He can't sing. The same conviction runs through her Benedictine world, where monks and nuns sang their prayers through the day instead of only saying them. In time the ban was lifted and her nuns sang again.
And her songs are still sung by choirs and monastic communities.
If a piece of music has ever sounded like a memory of somewhere you've never been, Hildegard would call it a memory of paradise.

how: Benedictine monks and nuns sing the Divine Office, the hours of prayer, through the day; choirs and some monastic communities sing Hildegard's chants, and the Ordo Virtutum is still staged.

o: her songs, where praise echoes heaven and the Devil can't sing
soft background chants written only for private prayer
folk songs she gathered from villages along the Rhine

p: her sung drama of the Virtues
the one part that never sings
no Mass and no singing for her nuns

s: in Hildegard's play the Devil gets the most dramatic song
he gets no song at all. every other part is sung; he only shouts.
Hildegard's community was once forbidden to sing
after she refused to have a buried man dug up, her house was put under an interdict until the ban was lifted.
for Hildegard, music in worship was a pleasant extra
she wrote that music is how people remember and rejoin the harmony lost in paradise.

games.q: your cousin's school cuts its choir to save money and she says, 'it's just singing.' what would Hildegard's letter say about praise that gets silenced?
o: song is more than extra: for her, it was how people rejoin a harmony they'd lost.
she'd agree: singing is pleasant, but it can be dropped without much loss.
she'd say only monks and nuns should sing, so the choir doesn't matter.
games.why: when her nuns were forbidden to sing, Hildegard wrote that music echoes paradise and that silencing it without cause is the Devil's kind of work.

practice: Find a recording of one of Hildegard's chants, O viridissima virga or any other, and listen with nothing else open. If no recording is near, hum one long, low note on each out-breath and let it fill your chest.

wordCard.voice: Hildegard's music: her chants and her sung drama of the Virtues, where praise is heaven's harmony and only the Devil can't sing.
